description: Fig. 4 is a single-panel powder X-ray diffraction pattern of the PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder. The abscissa is 2θ (degree) with tick marks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100; the ordinate is Intensity (a.u.) and carries no numeric scale. A legend in the top-right corner defines black circles as γ-Fe(M) and red triangles as α-Fe(M). The trace is dominated by a very tall peak lying just below the midpoint of the 40–50° interval, labelled (111) and marked with a black circle; further black-circle reflections labelled (200), (220), (311) and (222) follow at successively higher angle, the last sitting near the middle of the 90–100° interval. Two small red-triangle peaks mark the α-Fe(M) phase: a weak (110) reflection immediately to the right of the dominant (111) peak, and a very weak (200) reflection near the middle of the 60–70° interval. The figure therefore demonstrates that the powder is predominantly fcc γ-Fe(M) austenite with a minor bcc α-Fe(M) ferrite fraction. No numeric intensity or d-spacing values are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a single XRD pattern with 2θ (degree) plotted from 30 to 100 on the abscissa with ticks at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100, and Intensity (a.u.) on the ordinate with no numeric scale.
The top-right legend defines black circles as γ-Fe(M) and red downward triangles as α-Fe(M).
Five black-circle reflections are labelled: (111), (200), (220), (311) and (222).
Two red-triangle reflections are labelled: (110) and (200).
The tallest peak in the pattern is the (111) γ-Fe(M) reflection, located between the 40° and 50° ticks, slightly below the midpoint of that interval; it is far more intense than every other peak.
The α-Fe(M) (110) peak sits immediately to the right of the dominant γ-Fe(M) (111) peak, between the 40° and 50° ticks, and is only a small shoulder-level peak.
The α-Fe(M) (200) peak is the weakest labelled feature and lies between the 60° and 70° ticks.
The γ-Fe(M) (220), (311) and (222) peaks lie in the 70–80°, 80–90° and 90–100° intervals respectively, with intensities far below the (111) peak.
No numeric intensity values, d-spacings, lattice parameters or peak positions in 2θ are printed anywhere on the pattern.
The caption states the figure is the XRD pattern of the PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder.
The citing text states the pattern shows diffraction peaks for both the γ-Fe(M) and α-Fe(M) phases, with γ-Fe(M) dominating.
The citing text attributes the dominance of γ-Fe(M) to relatively slow cooling of the PREP-prepared powder, with only a small amount of carbon dissolved in the α-Fe phase promoting ferrite formation.
